name: Galal
overview: Galal was a male Levite known primarily for being counted among those carried into exile, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:15. He was the son of Jeduthun and part of the tribe of Levi, which held special religious and priestly duties in Israel. Beyond his lineage and tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Galal is a proper name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 9:15, and it possibly means 'tortoise' or 'roll away.' This meaning is not explicitly connected to any divine naming but reflects a Hebrew root that may describe a characteristic or symbolic image.
familyAndRelationships: Galal was the son of Jeduthun, a relationship explicitly stated in 1 Chronicles 9:16. Additionally, it is inferred that Shemaiah was his father, also referenced in the same verse. Scripture thus records his immediate paternal lineage but does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Galal's significance lies in his inclusion among the Levites who were taken into exile, highlighting the continuity of the Levitical line even in times of national crisis. As a descendant of Jeduthun, a notable Levitical figure, Galal represents the preservation of the priestly heritage during the Babylonian exile. His mention underscores God's faithfulness to maintain His covenant people and their religious duties despite displacement.
